summary: Eight instruments must be rebuilt, including one the round-1 critic accepted as 'the best of the twelve'. Four of the five R1 rejections are materially repaired and journey-run is this round's best work. The repeated pattern is R1's inverted: R1 found tools that substituted PERMISSIVELY and passed; round 2 fixed the permissiveness by substituting RESTRICTIVELY and refusing. Three of the eight refuse a measurement the running build answers determinately, and one of those converts a live build failure into corpus_debt.
worst_instrument_why: Second round running. Its refusal REASON is true — the quest-offer path is genuinely race-invariant, which I confirmed by driving six character signatures through __HARNESS.questOffers() in the running build — but the CONCLUSION is false. The tool fabricates ctx.dispositions from a derived race ceiling; the shipping build's Engine.seedDispositions() (engine.js:4563) writes rec.disposition RAW and canOffer reads exactly that, so the tool models an offer gate the build does not have. Its flagship independent falsification (mint an npc record, 36 dunmer signatures go red at Q-DEEP-01) was reproduced and then driven through THE ENGINE on the same patched tree: the engine blocked nobody, and the disposition clause vanished for all five signatures. And the nine givers with no npc record are, in the running build, a hard race-invariant unpassable gate — a FAIL — which the tool reports as unmeasurable, charging corpus_debt where the build should be charged.
harness_state: node tools/harness/boot-check.mjs PASS before every measurement. Recorded because smoke.mjs never boots the engine, which is how a broken build once passed every check on this tree.

verified_claims: The quest-offer path IS race-invariant in the running build — CONFIRMED independently. Six signatures (dunmer/lukiul, dunmer/foreign-born, saxhleel/interior, saxhleel/lukiul, imperial/blackrose, nord/foreign-born) driven through __HARNESS.questOffers() after reset produce a byte-identical disposition-clause set and identical offerable counts.
The giver census is right: 0 of 40 givers with a disposition_min resolve to a reaction group; 9 have no npc record at all.
The tier-5 cohort now resolves from danger_tier == 5 and the war-brood is fought as a GROUP. The R1 substitution is gone and the false 'regions.json declares no tier' note is deleted.
--data-root is a real and useful falsification handle; I used it for the shadow-tree work.

defects.detail: questClearableInner() computes dispositionCeiling(...) and assigns ctx.dispositions = { [npc]: ceiling } before calling the shipping canOffer(). Engine.seedDispositions() writes q.dispositions[rec.id] = rec.disposition, raw, with no group/race/upbringing term. derivedDisposition() reaches the world in exactly two places in game/src — Engine.npcDisposition() (a read-only surface) and character/encounter.js openingFor() (encounter hostility). Neither is a quest gate.

defects.title: THE THIRD BUG — `needs` is a list of guesses the library never validates
defects.detail: surfaceSaysAbsent is an OR over 'is any name in spec.needs missing from the harness'. Nothing checks that a name in needs is a method the build would ever have. For 8 of the 12 shipped reporters EVERY name in needs is absent from the 322-method surface — getHeapSnapshot, gc, getHeapStats, getStreamingState, getResidentAssets, getResourceRegistry, getAssetManifest, getAudioStats, getAudioLog, audioState, musicState, getMusicLog, recordAudio — so the term is a CONSTANT TRUE and cannot fail. The EXIT 21 ARRIVED fuse, the entire reason these files are defensible rather than notes, is unreachable by construction for two thirds of them unless a future author picks the builder's guessed names exactly. Only the four Tier-H reporters rest on a live signal (getPerfStats()._unmeasurable / getLoadState()._unmeasurable). It went unnoticed because the builder's implemented-system falsification used 'gamepad', the one case where the method names are real.
defects.measured: reportAbsence({ system: 'a quest runtime', needs: ['questOffers','questBook','getQuestLedger'] }) -> ABSENT, exit 20, quoting 'the harness methods the real instrument needs are absent: getQuestLedger' — about a system I had just driven 69 quests through in the same pass.

defects.title: The substring->prefix fix over-corrected and now lies the other way
defects.detail: The build packs three absent systems into one not_implemented entry: 'heap/GC access (A-JRN9), dialogue state (A-JRN13), resource registry (A-JRN14). A-JRN2 (gamepad) and A-JRN4 ... landed with W1-08/W1-29 ...'. A prefix match makes buildSaysAbsent FALSE for dialogue state and resource registry — both genuinely absent and both named right there. Bug 1 said ABSENT while quoting 'it landed'; bug 4 says ARRIVED while quoting 'it is not implemented'. Neither matcher reads that entry as the list it is. Exit 21 is the 'go delete this file' code.
defects.measured: reportAbsence({ system: 'dialogue state', needs: ['getUIState','getRenderedText'] }) -> ARRIVED, exit 21, 'REPLACE IT with a real one'. Control: system 'gamepad' with real method names still returns ARRIVED/21 correctly, so the builder's own falsification holds — it just did not generalise.

rebuild_instructions: Validate every `needs` entry at startup against the live harness surface AND a declared source (the amendment id, HARNESS.md), and refuse loudly when a required name matches nothing and is not traceable to a named amendment.
Parse not_implemented[].what as a LIST of systems, not a string — or better, ask for a harness change emitting one entry per system.
Fail closed on ambiguity: ARRIVED must require positive evidence that the system works, not merely the absence of a declaration.

A single init script patching WebGLRenderingContext.prototype.getParameter turns SwiftShader into an RTX 4070 in the tool's own artifact and nothing notices. tools/lib/browser.mjs launches Chromium with --use-angle=swiftshader in DETERMINISTIC_CHROMIUM_ARGS, on the NODE side where the page cannot reach it, and the gate never consults it. referred_judgements.subject: RI-JRN07 §B strata Q2 and Q5 reported unimplementable as written
referred_judgements.ruling: GENUINE CONTENT GAP. Not a corpus defect in the strata themselves, and NOT a builder giving up.
referred_judgements.measured: Over all 69 shipped quests: 4 carry a rank_gate at all, min_rank values present [1,2], max 2 -> Q2 has 0 candidates. Quests with q.region set: 0. Quests with any destination field: 0 -> Q5 has 0 candidates.
referred_judgements.reasoning: The builder undersold it. It is not that q.region is 'set on almost no quest' — there is NO destination field of any kind on any quest. The only spatial information is giver.location and a free-text `directions` string. Q5's predicate cannot fire, ever, under this schema. Widening it to 'any quest with a long directions string' would be exactly the illegitimate substitution R1 ruled on, and the builder was right to refuse it.
referred_judgements.consequence: corpus_debt charged to CONTENT, not to the tool and not to any builder. Rule S1 makes the five binding, so RI-JRN07's instrumented pass is unmeasurable until Q2 and Q5 are populated.
referred_judgements.corpus_rider: §B Q5 asks for geometry ('>= 15 walk-minutes away, crossing a region border') while §C U1 requires 100% directions_coverage from the same information AS PROSE. One item wants that fact in two incompatible forms and ships neither the field nor a region-to-region walk table. File as a corpus defect alongside the content gap. The tool's phrasing should be corrected to 'no quest carries any destination-region field'.

referred_judgements.subject: RI-MTH06 §A's worked example not producible on shipped data by any correct tool
referred_judgements.ruling: CONFIRMED. It is a GAME defect, owned by game/src, and it is WORSE than reported. The builder's proposed fix would not work.
referred_judgements.measured: Six signatures through questOffers() in the running build: byte-identical disposition clauses. Then the builder's own remedy applied on a shadow tree — speaker-teel-ashaan minted with reaction_group RG-DEEP and disposition 50 — and the ENGINE booted on it: the offer gate did not move for any race; the disposition clause vanished for ALL five signatures, because seedDispositions() writes the raw 50 and never consults the matrix.
referred_judgements.reasoning: The defect is not a missing field. It is that the reaction matrix is not wired to the quest path at all. derivedDisposition() reaches the world in exactly two places in game/src — Engine.npcDisposition() (a read-only surface) and character/encounter.js openingFor() (encounter hostility). No quest gate calls it. Adding reaction_group to 31 records would make build-viability go red for race-gated blocks THE GAME DOES NOT HAVE — strictly worse than today.
referred_judgements.dispatch_correction: orchestration/NEXT-DISPATCH.md §1b must be amended. The fix belongs in one of two places: seedDispositions() applies derivedDisposition() against the character, or canOffer/_dispositionToward derive at read time. Either is a few lines. The data work (records + reaction_group fields) is NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT, and dispatching it alone would produce a build that still ignores race while every instrument reported that it did not.
referred_judgements.nuance_in_the_build_s_favour: Race is not wholly inert. openingFor() gates encounter hostility on the matrix, so a Dunmer and a Saxhleel can be MET differently in the world. It is the QUEST path that is blind. _dispositionToward() also carries a sap-taint term that non-Argonians accumulate — a race-correlated penalty, but earned through play, not a creation-time bar, and it touches resolutions rather than offers.
